plans.note: Section 7 is captioned 'Limitations of Liability' — check cap amount, mutuality (heading suggests it may protect Contractor only) and carve-outs for IP infringement, confidentiality, gross negligence.

Section 7 expressly provides 'Indemnification of Contractor' — wrong direction; confirm whether any Contractor-to-Clear Capital IP/misconduct indemnity exists (possibly tied to the warranties in Section 5) and whether our indemnity to Contractor is unacceptably broad.
No restrictive-covenant section in the outline; scan Section 1 (Purpose of Engagement) for any limits on the businesses we operate or competing products we may buy or build.
Exclusivity would most likely be embedded in the scope/purpose language in Section 1 or the compensation terms in Section 3; otherwise absent, which is acceptable to us.
Pricing sits in Section 3; check for any obligation on us to offer Contractor best terms. An MFN in our favour is welcome and would not be flagged.
No standalone covenants section; non-solicits are sometimes tucked into the termination or engagement sections. If present and binding on us, test duration, scope and general-advertising carve-out.
Section 6 (Termination) is the controlling clause — confirm we may terminate on notice without penalty and that Contractor cannot walk away mid-engagement on equal terms.
Term/renewal mechanics would appear in Section 6 or the engagement description in Section 1; if there is no auto-renewal, the rule is satisfied by absence.
No miscellaneous/general provisions section appears in the outline; check the preamble and the tail of Section 7 for a choice-of-law or arbitration clause before concluding it is missing.
No assignment section listed; look in the preamble (successors/assigns language) and Section 6 for a change-of-control termination trigger against us.

Section 4 governs ownership of materials related to the Services — confirm work product and our data vest in Clear Capital and that no Clear Capital IP is assigned or licensed to Contractor beyond performance needs.
Any licence-back or retained-rights grant will sit in Section 4; test affiliate/contractor coverage and whether the grant is revocable at will.
Audit/records-inspection language, if any, would ride with the compensation terms in Section 3; check frequency, notice, location and cost allocation if present.
Look for late-payment penalties, kill fees or liquidated damages payable by us in Section 3 and in the liability provisions of Section 7.

Section 5 contains Contractor's warranties plus a disclaimer — test warranty duration and remedy against the Specifications, and read with the acceptance mechanic in Section 4; the disclaimer may gut the warranty.
No insurance section in the outline; Contractor is on-site/data-touching, so if nothing appears in Section 5 or elsewhere the rule is missing.
Check Section 3 for minimum fees, guaranteed hours or take-or-pay commitments and whether Section 6 provides an exit from them.
Section 6 may address post-termination effects and Section 4 the return/delivery of materials; if neither provides data return and transition assistance, flag as missing.
